Practice note · editorial draft

AI in research: organise, then verify

A framework for using AI as a research assistant while keeping control of sources and findings.

AI can help research through clearly defined tasks: refining a question, structuring a literature review, proposing a coding plan or clarifying an explanation. Response quality depends on the context and documents provided.

A suggested source remains a lead until checked in the original document. Its existence, authors, date and the passage supporting the argument must be verified. A plausible reference is not a verified reference.

For analysis, a script must be executed and checked. Units, missing observations, variable construction and model selection remain the researcher’s decisions. A well-explained coefficient does not become more valid.

Useful practice therefore retains a record of decisions, code and limitations. AI can speed up preparation and communication; responsibility for interpretation and validation remains human.

About this note

Editorial text prepared for this portfolio, to review before public release. It makes no claim of an empirical study or technical implementation.
